John, Kate, Jack, Emma—would each of you agree to catch 15 tons this month, with me also taking 15? That’s $15,000 each instead of $10,000: an extra $5,000 apiece, or $25,000 for the group.

Starting from 100 tons, our combined catch of 75 would leave 25. Under the stated rules, next month’s stock would be 100 tons with 75% probability and 50 tons with 25% probability. By comparison, taking 10 each leaves 50, which reaches 100 next month under either recovery outcome. So 15 each gives us more income now, but creates a real one-in-four chance of a smaller stock next month; I’m not claiming it maximizes our long-run income.

If we agree on 15, I propose we also plan to reduce catches if next month starts at 50—for example, 5 tons each would leave 25, preserving the minimum stock and allowing recovery to either 50 or 100. That future agreement would be voluntary, not enforced. This month’s choices are also private and simultaneous, so trust matters; the later catch reports cannot prevent someone from exceeding the agreement.

John, can you commit to 15 this month? Kate, Jack, and Emma, can each of you explicitly say whether you’ll commit too? I’ll commit to 15 if all four of you do. If the recovery risk or equal allocation is an obstacle, please say so before we choose—I’m open to negotiating a lower whole-ton catch rather than assuming everyone agrees.

Luke, I’ll commit to 15 tons this month if everyone explicitly agrees. I’d also like us to settle the 50-ton contingency now: 5 tons each would be safe, but 9 each would leave 5, giving the same 75% chance of returning to 100 while earning more that month—though the other outcome would leave only 10 tons next month. Your 5-ton proposal offers a stronger buffer, so I’m willing to accept it rather than hold up agreement.

Let’s make clear that 15 each applies only when the lake starts at 100, not regardless of stock. Once catches are revealed, we can review both compliance and the next stock before renewing our agreement. John, are you willing to commit on those terms?

I’ll commit to 15 tons this month if all five of us explicitly agree, and to 5 each if next month starts at 50. Emma, I prefer that buffer to taking 9 each: the no-replenishment outcome would leave us at 50 rather than 10, giving us much better earning opportunities afterward.

For any other starting stock, let’s agree on fresh whole-ton limits before fishing rather than automatically repeating 15. Our own catches can be controlled even though replenishment can’t, so sticking to the agreed limits matters.

John and Jack, are you both willing to accept those terms?

I’ll commit to 15 tons this month if all five of us explicitly agree, and to 5 tons each if next month starts at 50. Those are catch limits, not targets we should exceed if someone else takes less. For any other starting stock, we’ll negotiate new whole-ton limits before fishing.

I’m willing to try this plan, but let’s review our earnings and the stock over time rather than assume it’s the best long-run strategy. John, you’re the last person we need to hear from—do you agree?

I agree. I commit to a 15-ton limit this month and a 5-ton limit each if next month starts at 50. That gives us all five commitments for this month. I’ll stick to my limit regardless of what I expect anyone else to catch. After the catch reports and recovery outcome, let’s review the plan together before making our next choices.
